name: PORTUGAL
lead: Portugal sits at the western edge of Europe, where the Atlantic begins. Its sailors once mapped half the globe. Today 260 million people speak Portuguese. Its borders have barely changed since 1139.

facts.label: High point
facts.sub: Volcano on Azores island of Pico

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Portugal runs down the west side of the Iberian Peninsula. It has 832 km of Atlantic coast. The north is green and rainy. The south is sunny, with golden cliffs.
Far out at sea lie the Azores, volcanic islands 1,500 km west. Madeira island is closer to Morocco than Lisbon. Mount Pico, Portugal's highest peak, is a sleeping volcano.
animals: The Iberian lynx prowls cork-oak forests on big paws. In 2002, fewer than 100 were left. Breeding brought them back to over 1,600 in Portugal and Spain.
The Iberian wolf has striped legs and hunts in small packs north of the Douro River. About 300 live in Portugal. A law has protected them since 1988.
culture: Blue-and-white azulejo tiles cover churches and houses. Moorish rulers began this tradition 500 years ago. Fado is music full of saudade, a longing for something you cannot name.
Benfica, Porto, and Sporting are old football rivals. Lisbon monks invented pastéis de nata, tiny custard tarts, in the 1800s. Millions eat them daily.
history: Portugal became a kingdom in 1139. In the 1400s, its sailors began the Age of Discovery. Vasco da Gama reached India by sea. Pedro Álvares Cabral landed in Brazil. The empire spanned four continents.

In 1755, an earthquake flattened Lisbon and sent a tsunami (giant wave) across Europe. The city was rebuilt in a grid within years. In 1974, the Carnation Revolution ended a dictator's rule peacefully.
wows: Portugal makes half the world's cork, peeled by hand every nine years.
Lisbon was founded around 1200 BC, four centuries before Rome.
In early 2025, clean energy made over 80% of Portugal's power over three months.
Livraria Bertrand in Lisbon, open since 1732, is the world's oldest bookshop.
Portugal's borders are the oldest in continental Europe.
Portuguese is official in nine countries on four continents.
In 1974, a peaceful revolution filled soldiers' rifle barrels with flowers.

myths.myth: Lisbon is built on flat land
myths.fact: Lisbon sits on seven hills. Yellow trams climb its steep streets.

myths.myth: Portuguese is just Spanish with an accent
myths.fact: They share Latin roots but sound very different. Many Spanish speakers cannot follow spoken Portuguese.
